about: The three sample questions of the lesson page. Written by us (not from the course homework). Each answer is marked by exact quotes from the CS 156 captions; build_m3_input.py checks that every quote occurs in the chunk text. Q1 is D1 of the chunking page. Q2 tests an exact acronym, Q3 is a paraphrase of Q1 with few shared words. Answer marking is ours (one rater).

questions.question: Why is a bigger margin better for generalization?
answer_quotes: If you have the bigger margin, the chances are the new point will still be on correct side of the line.
Fat margins imply fewer dichotomies possible.
questions.why_this_one: A natural question that shares its key words with the lecture (margin, bigger, better).

questions.question: What does KKT stand for?
answer_quotes: Karush, which is the first K, and Kuhn-Tucker, which is the KT.
questions.why_this_one: An exact acronym: one rare token carries the question, the textbook case for keyword search. See whether it wins.

questions.question: Why does leaving a wide empty gap between the two classes help the classifier on unseen data?
answer_quotes: If you have the bigger margin, the chances are the new point will still be on correct side of the line.
Fat margins imply fewer dichotomies possible.
questions.why_this_one: Q1 said in other words: it shares almost no rare word with the answer, which suits a dense embedding.
